2. In Civil Revision No.2458 of 2007 preferred by the defendant-respondent-petitioners, the Rule was issued calling upon opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 29-3-2007 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chattogram in Other Appeal No.80 of 1988, allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 31-12-1987 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Potiya, Chattogram in Other Suit No.210 of 1984, dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper, should not be passed. Pending the disposal of the Rule, the operation of the impugned judgment and decree dated 29-3-2007 passed in Other Appeal No.80 of 1988 was stayed. 

 3. In Civil Revision No.3400 of 2007 preferred by the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner, the Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 29-3-2007 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chattogram in Other Appeal No.80 of 1988, allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 31-12-1987 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Potiya, Chattogram in Other Suit No.210 of 1984, dismissing the suit should not be modified in terms of the reliefs prayed for in the plaint and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper, should not be passed. 

 4. In Civil Revision No.2459 of 2007 preferred by the defendant-respondent-petitioner, the Rule was issued calling upon opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 29-3-2007 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chattogram in Other Appeal No.81 of 1988, reversing the judgment and decree dated 31-12-1987 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Potiya, Chattogram in Other Suit No.14 of 1985, dismissing the suit should not be set-aside and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper, should not be passed. Pending the disposal of the Rule, the operation of the impugned judgment and decree dated 29-3-2007 passed in Other Appeal No.81 of 1988 was stayed. 

 5. In Civil Revision No.3401 of 2007 preferred by the plaintiff-appellant-petitioner, the Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 29-3-2007 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Chattogram in Other Appeal No.81 of 1988, allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 31-12-1987 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Potiya, Chattogram in Other Suit No.14 of 1985, dismissing the suit should not be modified in terms of the reliefs as prayed for in the plaint and/or why such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper, should not be passed. 

 One Satya Ranjan Singha, Chairman of Shreeguru Sangha, Rhishidham at Jangal Kokdandi, Police Station-Banshkhali, District-Chattogram filed for himself and on behalf of all the saints, disciples and votaries thereof Other Suit No.89 of 1979 renumbered as Other Suit No.210 of 1984 in the representative form under Order 1 Rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Chattogram for the following reliefs: 

 7. The plaintiff claimed that Pulin Bihari Datta owned the land in Schedule 1 and some other land and that he was a devout person. He orally donated 3.00 acres of his 6.40 acres of land to Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj, the spiritual son of Shree Swami Jagadananda Puri Maharaj, in 1948 for the purpose of establishing a religious organisation and spreading Baishnabism. The Swami accepted the donation and took possession of the land. Later, on 17-10-1949, Pulin Bihari Datta executed and registered a deed of gift to confirm the previous oral donation. However, the brothers of Pulin Bihari Datta claimed interest in the donated properties, and as a result, the revenue payment of the total land of 6.40 acres was defaulted. The land was then auctioned and purchased by Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj in Certificate Case No.260 of 1950-51 for Rhishidham, the religious organisation. He obtained the sale certificate and delivery of possession. In addition, Surendra Lal Kulal also donated 2.00 acres of land to Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj for Rhishidham by a deed of gift on 20-5-1957 for the benefit and use of the saints, disciples and followers of the Guru under the guidance of Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj. Thus, Rhishidham acquired 8.42 acres of land and some other lands in Schedule 1 under the absolute guidance of Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj. While Sadananda Puri was the Mohanta and Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj was the spiritual leader of Rhishidham, Sadananda Puri took settlement of 13.32 acres of land in Schedule 2 from the Government on 28-1-1967 through Settlement Case No.35 of 1960-61 for the propagation and spread of Baishnabism. Thus, the lands in Schedules I and 2 became the exclusive properties of Rhishidham under the care and religious leadership of Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj, who had no personal interest in the said properties, nor did he treat the same as such. Though the title of the properties belongs to Rhishidham, Shreeguru Sangha was established on 15-6-1962 by Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj with the disciples and votaries of Rhishidham to manage and maintain all the aforesaid properties of schedule-1 and 2. Thus, the suit properties are the exclusive properties of Shreeguru Sangha for Rhishidham and the same were acquired for its interest, use and enjoyment as well as for the propagation of Baishnabism in the world. Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj died on 15-4-1966. Thereafter in 1967, Sadananda Puri Maharaj breathed his last. On his death, Ashram's mother, Noni Gopal Brahmacharini of Shreeguru Sangha Rhishidham was made Mohanta in place of Sadananda Puri Maharaj. Accordingly, she had been performing all the religious duties of the Ashram to the satisfaction of all the said disciples and votaries but, said Noni Gopal died on 6-2-1987. Thereafter, Sadhonananda Puri Maharaj was nominated and appointed Mohanta of the Ashram/Rhishidham. During the BS operation, the land acquired by Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj was recorded in his name on behalf of Rhishidharn and the land acquired by Rhishidham itself was recorded in the name of Sadananda Puri on behalf of Rhishidham. Accordingly, they never used the suit land as their personal property. On the other hand, defendant No.1, who was a married person and died recently, filed an application before the then Sub-Divisional Court in 1972 claiming that he obtained the properties of Schedule 1 from his brother Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj as his heir and also procured a Muktinama from Mahanta Sadananda Puri in respect of the properties of Schedule 2, which are false. Moreover, as the properties belong to Rhishidham, Mahanta Sadananda Puri had no legal authority to transfer the same by issuing any such a Muktinama or otherwise. As Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj became a priest, his family relationships ceased, and the law of succession under the Daibhaga School of Law does not apply to his insurance. The BS record was wrongly recorded in the names of 12 persons as at that relevant they were found there and on 20-5-1978, a compromise took place between the Shreeguru Sangha Rhishidham and the saints, who admitted the title of Shreeguru Sangha Rhishidham. The Rhishidham Kumbha Mela, which has been held since 1962 corresponding to 1969 BSS for four days in every month of Magh or Falgun, could not take place in 1977 and 1978 as deceased defendant No.1 created obstacles, which gave rise to Other Suit No.17 of 1978 in the then 2nd Court of Sub-Judge, Chattogram. As the defendants denied the title of the plaintiff, he was constrained to file the suit. 

 9. Defendant No.4 also contested the suit by filing a separate written statement denying the material claim and allegations made in the plaint. His specific case, in short, is that earlier the plaintiff filed Other Suit No.17 of 1978 for permanent injunction in which he failed up to the High Court Division and the suit was lastly dismissed on 23-3-1983 and accordingly, the present suit is barred by res judicata. Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj was the spiritual preceptor of Rhishidham. After his death, the Rhishidham devolved on his brother as per the Hindu Law. Accordingly, his brother Achyutananda maintained the Ashram. After his death, his heirs are entitled to the maintenance of the Ashram. Accordingly, the plaintiff or Shreeguru Sangha cannot claim the title of the properties of Rhishidharn. 

 11. After hearing both the parties, the Trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 31-12-1987 (decree signed on 7-1-1985) dismissed the suit. 

 12. Against the judgment and decree of the Trial Court, the plaintiff preferred Other Appeal No.80 of 1988 before the learned District Judge, Chattogram and the appeal was transferred to the 1st Court of the learned Additional District Judge, Chattogram for its disposal. 

 13. In the meantime, the same plaintiff instituted Other Suit No.14 of 1985 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Potiya, Chattogram praying for the reliefs: 

 17. Upon hearing both the parties, the learned Trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 31-12-1987 (decree signed on 7-1-1988) dismissed the suit. 

 18. Against the judgment and decree of the Trial Court, the plaintiff preferred Other Appeal No.81 of 1988 before the learned District Judge, Chattogram and the appeal was transferred to the 1st Court of the learned Additional District Judge, Chattogram for its disposal. 

 19. Other Appeal Nos.80 and 81 of 1988 were heard analogously and by the judgment and decrees dated 29-3-2007 (decrees signed on 5-4-2007) the appellate Court allowed both the appeals, reversed the judgments and decrees of the trial Court and thereby decreed both the suits. 

 21. On the other hand, as the Court of Appeal below did not specify all the reliefs in the ordering portion as were prayed for in the plaints, the plaintiff of both the suits filed Civil Revision Nos. 3400 and 3401 of 2007 against the judgment and decrees passed in Other Appeal Nos. 80 and 81 of 1988 respectively for modification of the judgment and decrees of the Court of Appeal below. 

 22. Having placed all four Civil Revisions, Mr Subrata Chowdhury along with Ms Fatema Begum, Mr Md Mominul Islam and Mr Rabin Chandra Paul, learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioner in Civil Revision Nos.3400 of 2007 and 3401 of 2007 who is the plaintiff-opposite party in Civil Revision Nos.2458 of 2007 and 2459 of 2007 submits that upon meticulous examination and elaborate discussion of the material evidence on records, the Court of Appeal below found that the suit properties were acquired for establishing Rhishidham as well as for implementation of the religious thought and ideology thereof by Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj and, as such, under the law even, Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj was not legally authorized to claim the suit properties as his personal properties and for the same reason those are not biologically inheritable and accordingly, decreed rightly both the suits. The judgments and decrees of the Appellate Court contemplate that Sreeguru Sangha is an organisation of the devotees and votaries of Rhishidham, which was established by Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj while the plaintiff filed the suits in the representative form on his behalf and behalf of the similarly interested devotees and votaries. Having examined the material evidence on records, the Court of Appeal below rightly held that Shreeguru Sangha is the Managing Committee of Rhishidham comprising the nominated/elected devotees and votaries by and among themselves for managing and maintaining Rhishidham and that Sree Guru Sangha constitutes a 501-Member Organising Committee for arranging and holding the Kumbha Mela—an annual religious mass gathering of all devotees, votaries, followers and the people at large while even the defendants have not made out any case that there is any other collective forum of Rhishidham for those purposes; rather, they are claiming the suit property as of their own inherited from Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj as his reversioner heirs, which is not tenable in law. As the properties belong to Rhishidham, Mahanta Sadananda Puri had no legal authority to transfer the same by issuing any Muktinama or otherwise in favour of the defendant or anybody else. Since the defendants cannot claim any personal right to the suit properties, they have also no legal right to interfere with the suit properties and other affairs of Rhishidham and hence, the Rule issued in Civil Revision No.2458 of 2007 is liable to be discharged. The learned Advocate also submits that it has already been decided by the judgment and order dated 1-3-2012 passed in Writ Petition No.1163 of 2011 that by the order of the SZMLA, the defendants in the Government did not acquire any authority or title to control and manage the Rhishidham. The learned Advocate again submits that Shreeguru Sangha constitutes a 501-member Organizing Committee for holding and managing the Kumbha Mela yearly, but the Rhishidham is managed by Shreeguru Sangha and as per the will and intention of Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj, Shreeguru Sangha nominates the Sebayet, Mohanta or Mohanta Maharaj of Rhishidham and the same practice has been continuing since the lifetime of Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj. After the judgment and order dated 1-3-2012 passed in Writ Petition No.1163 of 2011, the UNO, Banshkhali-petitioner in Civil Revision No.2459 of 2007 had no legal authority to claim any right under the impugned order of the SZMLA, Bandarban which was declared to have issued without any lawful authority and was of no legal effect and accordingly, there is no merit in the Rule issued in Civil Revision No.2459 of 2007 and hence, the Rule is liable to be discharged. The learned Advocate lastly submits that since the Court of Appeal below decreed both the suits as a whole, it was required by law to specify all the reliefs prayed for and granted in both the suits and, as such, the Court of Appeal below without specifying the reliefs granted therein committed errors of law resulting in errors in the decision occasioning failure of justice and hence, both the Rules issued in Civil Revision Nos.3400 and 3401 of 2007 should be made absolute. 

 23. On the other hand, Mr Tapash Kumar Biswas learned Advocate for the petitioners in Civil Revision No.2458 of 2007 and opposite parties in Civil Revision No.3400 of 2007 submits that the defendant-petitioners do not claim any personal right in the suit properties but, they only claim the right to manage the suit properties as the heirs of Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj. The suit properties belonged to Rhishidham and not to Shreeguru Sangha while, in contradictory to his earlier submission, the learned Advocate further submits that all the devotees of Rhishidham are interested persons in the matters of Rhishidham and accordingly, they should manage the suit properties through the Sebayet and Mohanta. The plaintiffs failed to prove that Shreeguru Sangha was established as per the intention and ideology of Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj and, as such, the Trial Court rightly dismissed both the suits while the Court of Appeal below having misread the material evidence on record came to the erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice and hence, the Rules issued in Civil Revision No.2458 of 2007 should be made absolute while, the Rules issued in Civil Revision Nos.3400 of 2007 should be discharged. 

 24. I have perused all four Civil Revision Applications along with the records of the Court below and heard the learned Advocates from both sides. 

 25. Civil Revision No.2459 of 2007 has been preferred by Abu Fazal Md Rafiuddin, UNO, Banshkhali, Police Station- Banshkhali, District-Chattogram. It appears that this Civil Revision has not been filed with any authority of the Government nor through the office of the learned Attorney-General but, through a private Advocate of this Court and, as such, the same has been filed in the personal capacity of Abu Fazal Md Rafiuddin but his designation was at that time "UNO, Banshkhali". So, the petitioner here is a persona designata but, it appears from the plaint as well as from the decree passed in Other Suit No.14 of 1985 that UNO, Banshkhali was impleaded therein in his/her official capacity but, the Civil Revision has not been filed by the UNO, Banshkhali in the exercise of his official power and authority. Therefore, Abu Fazal Md Rafiuddin having no personal interest nor any cause to be aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the Appellate Court in Other Appeal No.81 of 1988 is not tenable in law. Moreover, it has already been found that the impugned order issued by the SZMLA, Bandarban has already been declared to have been issued without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect by the judgment and order dated 1-3-2012 passed in Writ Petition No.1163 of 2011. Moreover, the petitioner is absent from prosecuting the Rule and accordingly for all the reasons stated above, the Rule issued in Civil Revision No.2459 of 2007 is liable to be discharged. 

 26. From the findings and observations made by the learned Trial Court in both Other Suit Nos.14 of 1985 and 210 of 1984 (former 89 of 1979), it appears that the suit properties belonged to Rhishidham and those are debottor properties. Thus, the defendant-petitioners in Civil Revision No.2458 of 2007 have no personal or inheritable interest in the properties of Rhishidham but, the defendant-petitioners have not yet been aggrieved by such findings and observations and thereupon it becomes conceded and admitted that the defendant-petitioners have no personal as well as inheritable interest in the properties of Rhishidham. Accordingly, they have also no right and authority to manage, supervise or control the suit properties or any matters of Rhishidham as the biological heirs of its founder Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj. These facts have also not been controverted by the learned Advocate in his submissions; rather, he has candidly supported this position of facts. The learned Advocate only has stressed the point that Shreeguru Sangha has no authority to manage and supervise the matters of Rhishidham which was also found by the Trial Court. 

 30. Thus, it appears from the documents specifically from Exhibit 3(ka) as were exhibited even without any objection on behalf of the defendant-petitioners that at least since 20-5-1957, the Rhishidham was being managed by and through Shreeguru Sangha. In addition, there are also some documents of various Courts such as, the plaints of Title Suit No.99 of 1970 renumbered as Title Suit No.71 of 1974 and Title Suit No.54 of 1974 renumbered as Other Suit No.130 of 1976 that Shreeguru Sangha was functioning and managing the affairs of Rhishidham since long before. 

 31. Nevertheless, it also appears from the letter dated 11-12-1966 issued by the then Mohanta, Shreemot Swami SadanandaPuri appointing Shreemati Nani Brahmacharini as the next Mahanta that even, he was performing his functions as the Mohanta per the decision of Shreeguru Sangha. The defendant-petitioners even did not make any attempt to prove that the said appointment letter was not issued by Shreemot Swami Sadananda Puri. But having misread all those documents, the Trial Court arbitrarily found that there is no document to show that Shreeguru Sangha was established at any time while, the Court of Appeal below having considered all those documents found the existence, performance and functions of Shreeguru Sangha. Therefore, the material records are the evidence to show that Shreeguru Sangha was established before 20-5-1957 while admittedly, Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj died in 1966. Therefore, Shreeguru Sangha was established long before the death of Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj. Accordingly, I also concurrently find with the Court of Appeal below that Shreeguru Sangha was established as per the intention, ideology and instance of Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj, and the same has still been functioning as such and is entitled to manage and maintain all the affairs and properties of Rhishidham, which also include Tulsidham at Nandankanan, Chattogram as per Clauses 22 and 24 of "শ্রীশুরু সংঘ বিধি উপবিধি”, Exhibit-1. 

 32. On the contrary, it appears from the `Muktinama', Exhibit '71' that even if it were issued by Mahanta Sadananda Puri he did not get any approval of Shreeguru Sangha in issuing such Muktinama while, neither the Mohanta nor even Shreeguru Sangha had any legal right or authority to transfer any properties of Rhishidham except for the benefit and welfare of Rhishidham. In the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Abdul Hye and others, 2016 (24) BLT (AD) 340, it has been held, "a Shebait cannot delegate his duties to another, no matter whether such other is a stranger or a co-trustee on the principle of the maxim `Delegates non potestdelegare'." Therefore, the Mohanta had no legal authority to issue such a `Muktinama' transferring or delegating the properties or the managing authority of Rhishidham to the defendant-petitioners. It is a long-established principle of law that such religious properties or debottar properties or the properties of any religious trust cannot be transferred except for the benefit and welfare of the deity or the trust as the case may be. This principle gets support from the case of Basappa vs Shivagangawwa, ILR 1988 KAR 1246. It is another settled principle of law that if the Sebayet, Mohanta or even the Managing Committee does any act or takes any proceeding, it would not have any binding effect on the subsequent Sebayet, Mohanta or the Managing Committee since any action of the Sebayet, Mohanta or the Managing Committee is enforceable only during the tenure when they are or it is in their office. Such principle was laid down in the cases of Iswar Kalimata vs Manager Bijni Raj Court of Wards, AIR 1952 Cal 387 and Vidya Varuthi Thirtha vs Balusami Ayyar (1922) 24 BOMLR 629. In the case of Gopalakrishnan vs Cochin Devaswom Board and others, AIR 2007 3162 at paragraph 10 it was held as follows: 

 "10. The properties of deities, temples and Devaswom Boards, require to be protected and safeguarded by their Trustee/ Archks/Sebaits /employees. Instances are many where persons entrusted with the duty of managing and safeguarding the properties of temples, deities and Devaswom Boards have usurped and misappropriated such properties by setting up false claim of ownership or tenancy, or adverse possession. This is possible only with the passive or active collusion of the concerned authorities. Such acts of 'fences eating the crops' should be dealt with sternly. The Government, members or the trustees of Boards/Trust, and devotees should be vigilant to prevent any such usurpation or encouragement. It is also the duty of Courts to protect and safeguard the properties of religious and charitable institutions from wrongful claims or misappropriation". 

 In the present case, the defendant-respondent-petitioners initially claimed their title in the debottor properties by inheritance from Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj and then, on the strength of the said Muktinama and now, they are claiming only the managerial authority of the debottor properties in the same ways, which is not tenable in the given findings and observations. Moreover, the Courts also must protect and safeguard the debottor properties from the defendant-petitioners since the same has been managed and maintained by Sreeguru Sangha from the lifetime of its founder Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj. 

 34. In such facts and circumstances, the Court of Appeal below allowed both appeals. It appears from both the judgments and decrees passed by the Court of Appeal that therein no reliefs as sought by the plaintiffs were dismissed or rejected either expressly or by any findings and observations. Therefore, the decrees passed by the Court of Appeal below are legally deemed to be the decrees as a whole but, from the ordering portions of the respective judgments or the decrees passed therein, it appears that the decrees were not drawn in respect of all prayers made in the respective plaints. 

 35. Explanation 5 of section 11 stipulates that if any relief claimed in the plaint which is not expressly granted by the decree shall for the purpose of this section be deemed to have been refused. Therefore, all the reliefs prayed for in the respective plaint being not expressly granted by the respective judgments or decrees are deemed to have been refused by the Appellate Court although there are no such negative findings and observations in the respective judgments. Thus, the petitioner in Civil Revision Nos.3400 of 2007 and 3401 of 2007 has rightly preferred the respective Civil Revisions. It has already been found that Shreeguru Sangha is the organisation of all the devotees and followers of Swami Adwaitananda Puri Maharaj or Rhishidham and it has been functioning since at least 20-5-1957 and therefore, the defendant-petitioners have no right and authority to deal with the management of Rhishidham as of inheritable right. However, the defendant-petitioners are also entitled to be members/Sangha Santan of Shreeguru Sangha if they are the disciples of the Rhishidham and also may be part of management if are elected to the Executive Committee of Shreeguru Sangha by the Sangha Santans. Therefore, as per the findings and observations made in the judgments and decrees of the Court of Appeal below, the suits ought to have been decreed expressly in respect of all reliefs sought in the respective plaints. 

 38. Accordingly, both the judgments and decrees passed by the Court of Appeal below are to be modified upon specifying all the reliefs sought in the plaints. 

 39. Therefore, Other Suit No.210 of 1984 (previously, 89 of 1979) are hereby decreed as a whole upon modification of the decrees of the Appellate Court as follows: 

 Send down the records of the Courts below at once.
